planting.note: Root softwood cuttings in early summer, or plant container-grown shrubs in well-drained, average to fertile soil in full sun to partial shade in spring or fall; like other weigelas it blooms on old wood, so prune immediately after flowering rather than in late winter.

directions: Plant in full sun to light shade in well-drained soil, and prune out a portion of the oldest flowered canes right after bloom to keep the large, broad-leaved habit from becoming leggy. This Japanese species is grown for its distinctive two-toned display: the funnel-shaped late-spring flowers open pale pink to white and age to deep rose-carmine, so paler new blooms and darkening older ones appear together on the same branch. It is one of the larger, coarser-textured weigelas, with broad rounded leaves and an arching, spreading habit better suited to a shrub border or screen than a tight foundation planting. Established plants tolerate heat and a range of soils well but, like other weigelas, need consistent moisture while young to form a strong root system.
sources: Dirr's Manual of Woody Landscape Plants

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early spring or fall in well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun; established plants need a real winter chill period to flower well.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, near-neutral soil, and prune lightly right after bloom to remove spent flower clusters since next year's buds form soon after. This naturally compact Chinese species produces abundant small, fragrant lavender-purple flower panicles in mid-spring on a dense, twiggy, rounded shrub with small, fine-textured leaves that give it a tidier silhouette than common lilac. It has good resistance to powdery mildew and does not produce the leggy, bare-at-the-base growth that often afflicts larger lilacs, so it needs only minimal corrective pruning. Its compact scale and reliable floral display have made it a parent of several popular dwarf lilac cultivars, though the species itself remains a sound, lower-maintenance choice for foundation plantings and borders.
